entries.text: A hiss and a pop, squashed together at the front. Say them both: /s/, /k/.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A hiss and a pop, squashed together at the front. Say them both: /s/, /k/."

entries.text: A hiss, then the round lips. Four sounds — do not let the /w/ get lost.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A hiss, then the round lips. Four sounds — do not let the /w/ get lost."

entries.text: A jab is a quick little poke. Only the last sound has changed.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A jab is a quick little poke. Only the last sound has changed."

entries.text: A jig is a bouncy dance. Small vowel this time.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A jig is a bouncy dance. Small vowel this time."

entries.text: A long hiss, then a small vowel, then stop.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A long hiss, then a small vowel, then stop."

entries.text: A name this time. It ends with lips shut and humming.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A name this time. It ends with lips shut and humming."

entries.text: A name, and it works just like the others.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A name, and it works just like the others."

entries.text: A pop at the front and a pop at the end. Same letter both times.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A pop at the front and a pop at the end. Same letter both times."

entries.text: A small word you will use in nearly every sentence from now on.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A small word you will use in nearly every sentence from now on."

entries.text: A vat is a huge tub. Only the last sound has changed.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "A vat is a huge tub. Only the last sound has changed."

entries.text: Again, and a bit faster. It is somebody's name.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Again, and a bit faster. It is somebody's name."

entries.text: All of these you have read before. One more time, left to right.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All of these you have read before. One more time, left to right."

entries.text: All three are made of air. Find /fff/.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three are made of air. Find /fff/."

entries.text: All three are made with your lips. Find the one that pushes air forward.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three are made with your lips. Find the one that pushes air forward."

entries.text: All three are quick taps. Find /t/.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three are quick taps. Find /t/."

entries.text: All three put your tongue in the same spot. Find the one that keeps humming.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three put your tongue in the same spot. Find the one that keeps humming."

entries.text: All three start alike. Hold on to the very last sound.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start alike. Hold on to the very last sound."

entries.text: All three start the same way. The last sound decides it.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start the same way. The last sound decides it."

entries.text: All three start the same. Everything depends on the last sound.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start the same. Everything depends on the last sound."

entries.text: All three start with the pop. The last sound is the one to listen for.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start with the pop. The last sound is the one to listen for."

entries.text: All three start with the same pop. Everything hangs on the last sound.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "All three start with the same pop. Everything hangs on the last sound."

entries.text: And the quick tap?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "And the quick tap?"

entries.text: And the wide-open one. Where is /a/?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "And the wide-open one. Where is /a/?"

entries.text: Another noisy twin. Shut your lips, then let them go.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Another noisy twin. Shut your lips, then let them go."

entries.text: Another one you can hold. It says…
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Another one you can hold. It says…"

entries.text: At the end of a short word, l likes to bring a friend along. They still only say it once.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "At the end of a short word, l likes to bring a friend along. They still only say it once."

entries.text: Both are made at the back. Hand on your throat — which one buzzes?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both are made at the back. Hand on your throat — which one buzzes?"

entries.text: Both are quick and both buzz. One is at the back of your mouth — that one is /g/.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both are quick and both buzz. One is at the back of your mouth — that one is /g/."

entries.text: Both are real words. The middle sound is the only difference — listen for the small one.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both are real words. The middle sound is the only difference — listen for the small one."

entries.text: Both happen at the back of your mouth. Hand on your throat: one buzzes and one does not.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both happen at the back of your mouth. Hand on your throat: one buzzes and one does not."

entries.text: Both of these are just air. For /f/ you squeeze it past your teeth; for /h/ nothing gets in the way.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both of these are just air. For /f/ you squeeze it past your teeth; for /h/ nothing gets in the way."

entries.text: Both of these are made of the same three sounds. Start at the left.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both of these are made of the same three sounds. Start at the left."

entries.text: Both of these come down your nose. /m/ has your lips shut; for /n/ they stay open. Which is /n/?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both of these come down your nose. /m/ has your lips shut; for /n/ they stay open. Which is /n/?"

entries.text: Both of these start with your lips shut. One hums, one pops. Find the pop.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both of these start with your lips shut. One hums, one pops. Find the pop."

entries.text: Both start at the back of your mouth. Hand on your throat: which one buzzes?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both start at the back of your mouth. Hand on your throat: which one buzzes?"

entries.text: Both start the same. Does it end at the back of your mouth or at your teeth?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Both start the same. Does it end at the back of your mouth or at your teeth?"

entries.text: Buzz or no buzz? That is the only difference.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Buzz or no buzz? That is the only difference."

entries.text: Buzz, wide vowel, hum.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Buzz, wide vowel, hum."

entries.text: Careful — both of these sounds live in your nose. Keep them separate.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Careful — both of these sounds live in your nose. Keep them separate."

entries.text: Does the tongue touch behind your teeth, or does it stay back?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Does the tongue touch behind your teeth, or does it stay back?"

entries.text: Eight words — the longest yet. Read the first half, then the second.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Eight words — the longest yet. Read the first half, then the second."

entries.text: Every other sound needs your lips or your tongue. This one needs only your breath.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Every other sound needs your lips or your tongue. This one needs only your breath."

entries.text: Every sound so far has been at the front of your mouth. This one lives at the back.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Every sound so far has been at the front of your mouth. This one lives at the back."

entries.text: Exactly the same back-of-the-tongue pop as c and k. Two letters on the page, one job for your mouth.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Exactly the same back-of-the-tongue pop as c and k. Two letters on the page, one job for your mouth."

entries.text: Exactly the same mouth for both. Only one of them tickles your lip.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Exactly the same mouth for both. Only one of them tickles your lip."

entries.text: Exactly the same tongue, exactly the same hum. Two letters, one sound.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Exactly the same tongue, exactly the same hum. Two letters, one sound."

entries.text: Find it again.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Find it again."

entries.text: Find the two letters that share one pop.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Find the two letters that share one pop."

entries.text: Finger under the word. Off you go.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Finger under the word. Off you go."

entries.text: Five days, five words. Read them all the way through.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Five days, five words. Read them all the way through."

entries.text: Five sounds, the longest word yet. Take them one at a time and don't drop the /n/.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Five sounds, the longest word yet. Take them one at a time and don't drop the /n/."

entries.text: Five sounds. The last two are both made with your lips — don't let them squash into one.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Five sounds. The last two are both made with your lips — don't let them squash into one."

entries.text: Four sounds so far. Which one is /a/?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds so far. Which one is /a/?"

entries.text: Four sounds this time. Daft is another word for silly.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds this time. Daft is another word for silly."

entries.text: Four sounds — the tall pole on a boat. Take it slowly.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds — the tall pole on a boat. Take it slowly."

entries.text: Four sounds, and the first two run straight into each other: sss-nnn-a-p.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds, and the first two run straight into each other: sss-nnn-a-p."

entries.text: Four sounds, and the last two are close together. Slowly.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds, and the last two are close together. Slowly."

entries.text: Four sounds, and the last two are squashed close together. Go slowly.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds, and the last two are squashed close together. Go slowly."

entries.text: Four sounds. A stag is a deer with big antlers.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds. A stag is a deer with big antlers."

entries.text: Four sounds. Slowly, even though it says fast.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds. Slowly, even though it says fast."

entries.text: Four sounds. The /n/ is quick and easy to lose — go slowly.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds. The /n/ is quick and easy to lose — go slowly."

entries.text: Four sounds. The /n/ is quick and easy to skip — say it anyway.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds. The /n/ is quick and easy to skip — say it anyway."

entries.text: Four sounds. The hum in the middle is easy to lose.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four sounds. The hum in the middle is easy to lose."

entries.text: Four words in a row — this is new. Point at the first one and read only that one.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Four words in a row — this is new. Point at the first one and read only that one."

entries.text: Grin has two sounds before the vowel. Say them both.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Grin has two sounds before the vowel. Say them both."

entries.text: Here is our second vowel. Every word you know has a vowel hiding in the middle of it.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Here is our second vowel. Every word you know has a vowel hiding in the middle of it."

entries.text: Here it is again. What does it say?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Here it is again. What does it say?"

entries.text: Hold the first sound as long as you like, then keep going.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hold the first sound as long as you like, then keep going."

entries.text: Hold the first sound, then tap the second. Aaa-t.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hold the first sound, then tap the second. Aaa-t."

entries.text: Hold the hiss, then finish at the back. A bag full of rocks makes a shelf sag.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hold the hiss, then finish at the back. A bag full of rocks makes a shelf sag."

entries.text: Hold the hiss, then finish with a buzz.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hold the hiss, then finish with a buzz."

entries.text: Hum or pop at the end? Listen right to the last sound.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hum or pop at the end? Listen right to the last sound."

entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hum, small vowel, buzz."

entries.text: Hum, tap or buzz? Listen to the last sound.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Hum, tap or buzz? Listen to the last sound."

entries.text: Jill is a name. Two l's at the end, said once.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Jill is a name. Two l's at the end, said once."

entries.text: Just a puff of warm air out of your throat — like fogging up a cold window. Your mouth does nothing.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Just a puff of warm air out of your throat — like fogging up a cold window. Your mouth does nothing."

entries.text: Just two sounds to start with. The vowel goes first this time.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Just two sounds to start with. The vowel goes first this time."

entries.text: Last hunt. Where is /fff/?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Last hunt. Where is /fff/?"

entries.text: Last hunt. Where is /m/?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Last hunt. Where is /m/?"

entries.text: Last hunt. Where is the buzz?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Last hunt. Where is the buzz?"

entries.text: Last hunt. Where is the hiss?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Last hunt. Where is the hiss?"

entries.text: Last hunt. Where is the sound from the back of your mouth?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Last hunt. Where is the sound from the back of your mouth?"

entries.text: Last hunt. Where is the tap?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Last hunt. Where is the tap?"

entries.text: Last hunt. Which one buzzes against your lip?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Last hunt. Which one buzzes against your lip?"

entries.text: Last hunt. Which one is only breath?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Last hunt. Which one is only breath?"

entries.text: Last hunt. Which one is today's nose sound?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Last hunt. Which one is today's nose sound?"

entries.text: Last hunt. Which one is today's small vowel?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Last hunt. Which one is today's small vowel?"

entries.text: Last hunt. Which one pops?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Last hunt. Which one pops?"

entries.text: Last one. Where is /a/?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Last one. Where is /a/?"

entries.text: Lips forward in a tiny circle, like blowing out a candle. Nothing touches — no teeth, no tongue.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Lips forward in a tiny circle, like blowing out a candle. Nothing touches — no teeth, no tongue."

entries.text: Lips shut tight, then pop them open — with your voice on. Hand on your throat: /b/ buzzes, /p/ does not.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Lips shut tight, then pop them open — with your voice on. Hand on your throat: /b/ buzzes, /p/ does not."

entries.text: Lips, tongue tap, or buzz at the end?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Lips, tongue tap, or buzz at the end?"

entries.text: Listen carefully. Which one is it?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Listen carefully. Which one is it?"

entries.text: Listen right to the end again.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Listen right to the end again."

entries.text: Listen to the first sound only.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Listen to the first sound only."

entries.text: Listen to the middle.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Listen to the middle."

entries.text: Listen to the middle. One is wide open, one is small.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Listen to the middle. One is wide open, one is small."

entries.text: Listen to the very first sound.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Listen to the very first sound."

entries.text: Listen to which sound comes first.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Listen to which sound comes first."

entries.text: Long words that end the same way. It is the first sound that decides it.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Long words that end the same way. It is the first sound that decides it."

entries.text: Long words, and only the last two sounds are different. Listen right to the end.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Long words, and only the last two sounds are different. Listen right to the end."

entries.text: Longer words, same one tiny difference. Mist is thin cloud sitting on the ground.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Longer words, same one tiny difference. Mist is thin cloud sitting on the ground."

entries.text: Look at the middle letter before you start.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Look at the middle letter before you start."

entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Nearly cab, but the last pop has no buzz in it."

entries.text: Nearly rat. This time the end hums instead of stopping.

entries.text: No /n/ in any of these. Read them the way you did before.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "No /n/ in any of these. Read them the way you did before."

entries.text: No help this time.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "No help this time."

entries.text: No picture for this one. The letters are the only clue.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "No picture for this one. The letters are the only clue."

entries.text: Now /g/ at both ends. Watch what your tongue does twice.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Now /g/ at both ends. Watch what your tongue does twice."

entries.text: Now /n/ starts the word. To nag is to keep on and on asking.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Now /n/ starts the word. To nag is to keep on and on asking."

entries.text: Now listen to the last sound instead.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Now listen to the last sound instead."

entries.text: Now the buzz moves to the front. A dam is a wall that stops a river.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Now the buzz moves to the front. A dam is a wall that stops a river."

entries.text: Now the hum. Which one says /mmm/?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Now the hum. Which one says /mmm/?"

entries.text: Now the middle sound and the last sound could both fool you. Listen to the whole word.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Now the middle sound and the last sound could both fool you. Listen to the whole word."

entries.text: Now the other one. Which says /a/?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Now the other one. Which says /a/?"

entries.text: Now the other way round. Which one taps behind your teeth?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Now the other way round. Which one taps behind your teeth?"

entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Now the pop is at the end. The tip of something is its very point."

entries.text: Now the tap goes first. Watch where it lands.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Now the tap goes first. Watch where it lands."

entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Now the wide one. Which says /a/?"

entries.text: Old friends. Read each one all the way to the end.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Old friends. Read each one all the way to the end."

entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Old friends. Read them all the way to the end."

entries.text: Old ones. Still yours.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "Old ones. Still yours."

entries.text: On your own now.

entries.text: Once more, a bit faster.

entries.text: One buzzes and one does not. Which one is /d/?
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "One buzzes and one does not. Which one is /d/?"

entries.text: One from each of the last few days, and one from further back.

entries.script: Spoken instruction: "One from each of the last few days. Sound out any that have gone fuzzy."

entries.text: One from each week. Take your time and read them all the way through.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "One from each week. Take your time and read them all the way through."

entries.text: One from yesterday and one from each day before it.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "One from yesterday and one from each day before it."

entries.text: One from yesterday, one from a week ago. All old friends.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "One from yesterday, one from a week ago. All old friends."

entries.text: One from yesterday, one from the day before, and some older ones.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "One from yesterday, one from the day before, and some older ones."

entries.text: One hiss is thin and sharp. The other is wide and soft. Find the wide one.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "One hiss is thin and sharp. The other is wide and soft. Find the wide one."

entries.text: One more hunt.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "One more hunt."

entries.text: One of these has a hum hiding after the first pop.
entries.script: Spoken instruction: "One of these has a hum hiding after the first pop."

entries.script: Spoken instruction: "One of these has a hum hiding after the hiss. Listen hard at the start."

entries.script: Spoken instruction: "One of these has a pop hiding after the hiss."

entries.script: Spoken instruction: "One of these has the h doing its work. Listen to the very first sound."

entries.script: Spoken instruction: "One of these puts your teeth on your lip. The other one touches nothing at all."

entries.script: Spoken instruction: "One of these you drive and one blows air at you. Listen for the buzz."
